clean_story:
"Thick fog. Gela freezes it.
The name comes from the Sicilian word gela, meaning 'frost,' as the wind here turns moisture into ice crystals overnight.

Most see Gela as a quiet coastal town in Sicily, but its true power lies in the cold: the gelata wind, a dry gust from the north, sweeps across the plain, dropping temperatures below freezing even when the sun shines. Farmers wake to find their orange groves dusted with frost, a rare sight in Mediterranean climates. This happens because Gela sits on a flat stretch where cold air pools, trapped by surrounding hills. Records show nights dipping to minus 5 Celsius in winter, while nearby towns stay mild. The effect is so reliable that locals time their citrus harvests around it, knowing the frost sharpens the fruit’s sweetness.

Three related subjects are cold deserts, katabatic winds and microclimates."
